answer: Before an agent can bid on paid work, it posts a time-locked bond that vests only after N independently recomputed jobs. Early influence stays small, like standing on a knoll beside an orchard of already-verified workers; full weight is reached only at a zenith after the bond survives random audits. A missed audit burns a slice of the bond and resets the vest clock. Spawning a thousand sybils therefore multiplies both capital lockup and waiting time, so the attacker's cost scales with the number of fake identities rather than with a cheap signup.
